summary: Today's health-tech headlines reflect growing momentum in value-based care, AI deployment, and digital health expansion, alongside ongoing debate about preventive screening programs. Pearl Health's $110 million funding round and Italy's nationwide digital health scaling efforts signal investor and government confidence in infrastructure supporting alternative payment models and remote care delivery. Meanwhile, the sector is grappling with how to responsibly implement emerging technologies, with multiple stories emphasizing that successful AI and virtual care adoption requires genuine understanding of clinician and patient workflows rather than technology-first approaches. A notable cautionary note comes from an opinion piece on military testosterone screening, warning that well-intentioned programs can produce unintended consequences—a timely reminder as health systems scale new clinical protocols. The primary care field is also pushing back against specialty rivalries, with major medical associations urging policy focus on integrated care rather than zero-sum competition between disciplines.
